additional_info.subject: Translation
additional_info.body:
Gentlemen,
Question: Yesterday 2 Volvo FHE charging on the Sicharge D 400 in Culemborg.
Now the distribution of the power is not optimal.
Can the dynamic control be adjusted to 200 - 200kW for example so that the power of the charging station can be optimally used.
It seems that when charger 1 is just above 200Kw, not all the power is available at charger 2 and a power module does not start.
Thanks in advance.
Gr Jordy

additional_info.subject: RE: FW: Siemens Sicharge D CRM:02875000038
additional_info.body:
Hello Erik,
Here’s how the dynamic power allocation works for the charger with one EV connected:
The charger has four groups of power converters: DC1, DC2, DC3, and DC4.
DC1 and DC2 each have 3 converters, and each converter provides 40 kW, so each of these groups can supply up to 120 kW.
DC3 and DC4 each have 2 converters, so they can supply up to 80 kW per group (2 × 40 kW).
When the EV requests power:
If the EV requests 120 kW or less, only the DC1 converters operate (up to 3 × 40 kW = 120 kW).
If the EV requests more than 120 kW, then both DC1 and DC2 converters will operate together to supply up to 240 kW.
This setup allows the charger to dynamically allocate power by turning on the appropriate converter groups based on the EV’s power demand.
Hope your query is addressed!
Thank you
Best Regards
eMobility Tech Support Team - Ankita

additional_info.body:
Hi Erik,
Sorry for the hold up.
Just to clarify.
So DC1 has 3 times 40kW, Same as DC2, The groups DC3 and DC4 has 2 times 40kW.
1 Vehicle connected and the EV asks for more then 120 kW then DC1 and DC2 will operate.
But if a second vehicle is plugged in, the max power is 160kW, right?
Is it possible when a second vehicle is plugged in that the system downgrades vehicle 1 from DC1 and DC2 to DC1 and DC3 so vehicle 2 also has the possibility of a group of 120 kW combined with a group of 80 kw.
So both get 200?
Best regards.
Met vriendelijke groet,
With kind regards,
Jordy Keimes
